text: Real-time chapter recap — twenty-five lessons, one continuous idea: how do you compute correct, timely answers over data that never stops arriving.

Eventstreams moved data from a source through transformations to a destination. Eventhouse and KQL databases gave that data somewhere built for streaming to land. And KQL itself let you actually ask questions of it — filtering, aggregating, joining, and two real ways to get data in, streaming or batch.

Real-time dashboards put live tiles in front of people. Three window shapes — tumbling, hopping, and session — each answered a different question. Watermarks and out-of-order handling made lateness a deliberate tradeoff instead of an accident. And eventstream transformations shaped data before it ever landed.

Activator turned a rule into a real action. Streamed CDC and data quality checks kept things in sync and caught bad data early. Comparing to databricks showed the same computer science under a different label. And lesson forty-one chained every piece into one working pipeline.
None of this complexity was arbitrary — it's what always-on actually requires. Next up: chapter three, production data engineering — running what you built, reliably, at scale.
